findings.evidence: `LineBundle/Class.lean:31` explicitly says inverses require the dual of an invertible sheaf, while `LineBundleClass X` and its `CommMonoid` instance are defined for arbitrary schemes; lines 371–380 introduce the group only under `[IsIntegral X]` via Cartier-divisor surjectivity.
findings.fix: Construct inverses from dual invertible sheaves in the line-bundle layer for arbitrary `X`, define the `CommGroup (LineBundleClass X)` instance there, and retain the Cartier result only to identify `𝒪_X(-D)` with the inverse of `𝒪_X(D)`.
findings.issue: `LineBundleClass.isUnit` and the resulting `CommGroup` instance require `[IsIntegral X]`, although line-bundle classes form a group for every scheme; this leaves the canonical Picard API under-generalized and ties it to Cartier divisors.

summary: The Cartier-divisor tensor law is naturally scoped, but the Picard group API is unnecessarily restricted to integral schemes.
